description: NOVA-LAB (Next-Gen Orbital Visionary Alliance) is an international youth research and engineering team innovating across space mission architecture, AI-driven autonomous systems, computational astrophysics, and cybersecurity. Recognized by aerospace experts at The Mars Society’s international design competition for our Mars habitat and Digital Twin engineering, we bridge space science and intelligent systems to solve complex challenges on Earth and beyond.
summary:
SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive 3D time-domain astrophysics platform and AI discovery engine built for NASA’s SPHEREx mission. It integrates WebGL 3D sky navigation (React Three Fiber) with an Astropy/FastAPI astrophysics pipeline and physics-informed machine learning to detect moving substellar objects, variable stars, and Planet X candidates.

Using multi-epoch infrared FITS data from NASA/IPAC IRSA and WISE cross-matched against Gaia DR3 and AllWISE, the app lets users compare epochs via Compare Slider, Auto-Blink, and Difference SNR shaders. This isolates proper-motion dipoles (WISE 0855, Barnard’s Star) from stationary variables (RW Aurigae). Meanwhile, a 2D-CNN separates real moving dipoles from cosmic rays, and a 102-band near-infrared spectrum analyzer (0.75–5.0 µm) identifies water ice and methane absorption to flag optical-blind, ultra-cold anomalies with shareable coordinate deep-links.

By automating spectroscopic and time-domain screening across massive all-sky surveys, SPHEREx Explorer enables astronomers and citizen scientists to uncover hidden outer Solar System worlds invisible to optical telescopes.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

SPHEREx Explorer is an end-to-end, time-domain astrophysics discovery platform designed to hunt for hidden substellar objects (such as ultra-cold brown dwarfs and Planet X candidates) and transient variable stars across NASA’s all-sky near-infrared surveys.

The system operates across three integrated layers:

1. Astrophysics Processing Pipeline (Astropy, reproject, photutils):

Ingests multi-epoch infrared FITS imagery from NASA/IPAC IRSA (SPHEREx DR1 & QR3) and NASA SkyView (WISE 3.4 µm and 4.6 µm), aligns frames in ICRS coordinates via WCS reprojection, subtracts local zodiacal sky backgrounds using CircularAnnulus aperture photometry, and generates Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) difference maps alongside 102-band near-infrared spectra (0.75–5.0 µm).

2. Physics-Informed AI Screening (PyTorch, Scikit-learn, NumPy):

- 2D-CNN Dipole Filter: Evaluates 16x16 pixel difference cutouts to distinguish true moving object dipoles (paired positive/negative lobes) from cosmic rays, detector artifacts, and stationary variable stars (monopoles).

- 102-Band Spectral Classifier & Teff Regressor: Identifies diagnostic molecular absorption bands—water ice (H2O at 3.05 µm), methane (CH4 at 3.32 µm), and CO/CO2 (4.45 µm)—while estimating effective surface temperature (Teff).

- Planet X Anomaly Detector: Combines an Isolation Forest model with physical priors—flagging targets that exhibit optical dropout in Gaia DR3 (optical-blind), ultra-cold temperatures (< 200 K), deep CH4 absorption, and measurable proper motion.

3. Interactive 3D Sky Viewport & 102-Band HUD (React Three Fiber, FastAPI):

Projects multi-depth celestial coordinates into an interactive WebGL 3D starfield equipped with Auto-Blink Comparator and Difference SNR Shader modes, paired with a real-time 102-band spectrum chart and shareable coordinate deep-links.

How Our Project Is Creative

- Astronomical Blink Comparator Reimagined in 3D WebGL: Inspired by Clyde Tombaugh’s historic blink comparator used to discover Pluto, we modernized the workflow into a 3D interactive shader environment where users can visually blink epochs or switch to diverging SNR shaders to spot moving dipoles instantly.

- "Optical-Blind" Cross-Matching Strategy: Rather than relying solely on brightness, our AI cross-matches infrared detections live against ESA Gaia DR3 and NASA AllWISE. Cold outer Solar System bodies emit virtually zero visible light; by treating Gaia non-detection + infrared proper motion as a primary discovery signal, the system isolates high-priority Planet X candidates automatically.

- Unified Benchmark Storytelling: Users can toggle seamlessly between four distinct physical regimes—WISE 0855-0714 (ultra-cold Y-dwarf), Barnard’s Star (high-proper-motion M-dwarf), RW Aurigae (stationary photometric variable star), and a Planet X Candidate (anomaly score 0.98)—or click coordinates to trigger live backend inference in under 45 ms.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Accelerating All-Sky Triage: SPHEREx maps hundreds of millions of objects across 102 spectral channels. Manual inspection of multi-epoch difference images is impossible at scale; our automated dipole + spectral anomaly pipeline filters out false positives and ranks high-value targets for follow-up observation.

- Democratizing Space Science (Citizen Science Ready): By translating complex multi-extension FITS cubes and WCS headers into an intuitive browser experience with shareable coordinate URLs, students, educators, and citizen scientists can participate directly in time-domain infrared discovery without specialized desktop software.

Key Engineering & Scientific Factors Considered

- Photometric & Astrometric Rigor: Accounted for background zodiacal light gradients via annular median subtraction and Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) noise estimation, paired with ASINH dynamic range stretching so both faint substellar objects and bright stars remain visible.

- False-Positive Rejection: Explicitly trained the 2D-CNN on synthetic cosmic rays, bad detector columns, and stationary variable monopoles so bright flaring stars (like RW Aurigae) are classified accurately as variable_star rather than false moving objects.

- Reliability & Verification: Built a 32-test automated verification matrix (pytest) validating astrophysics math, ML inference contracts, and REST API latency (< 45 ms), deployed on a unified multi-service cloud architecture with graceful catalog fallbacks.

Tools, Languages & Software Used

- Languages: Python 3, TypeScript, GLSL (Custom Shaders)

- Frontend & 3D Visualization: React, Vite, React Three Fiber (Three.js), Tailwind CSS, Recharts

- Backend & Astrophysics Pipeline: FastAPI, Pydantic, Astropy, reproject, photutils, astroquery, NumPy

- AI & Machine Learning: PyTorch, Scikit-learn (Random Forest & Isolation Forest)

- NASA & Astronomical Data Sources: NASA/IPAC IRSA (SPHEREx DR1 & QR3 via SIA2), NASA SkyView (WISE 3.4 µm & 4.6 µm FITS), ESA Gaia DR3 & AllWISE (via CDS VizieR)

- Deployment & Testing: Vercel Multi-Service Architecture, Git/GitHub, Pytest
